newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa tables exchange amendment bills.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa tables exchange amendment bills.

text.p: The South African Finance Ministry on Monday tabled bills to effect a number of largely technical amendments to the stock exchanges and financial markets control acts.
"They are mainly just to correct a number of technical errors. I don't think there is anything that reflects a major change of policy," said Financial Services Board official Barney Knoetze.
The bills propose to allow both stock exchanges and financial exchanges to advertise and canvass for business, rights currently held only by members.
"I don't think we're going to see any huge amount of stock exchange advertising, but this was in response to a request from the industry," Knoetze said.
The stock exchanges bill reinstates the right of the registrar to impose fines for the late submission of documentation.
"The provision for fines was allowed to lapse by mistake and it has now been replaced, but this time with a provision allowing a member to explain why he was late with documentation," said Knoetze.
Another clause in both bills extends the liability to inspection in terms of the Inspection of Financial Institutions Act from exchanges and members to investors suspected of manipulative practices.
Other amendments are minor, ranging from the correction of an "and" to an "or" to a fuller definition of the term "bona fide".
